exact.地圖是替代品 Surrogate，只保留與決策有關的結構，不是實地本身。: A map is a surrogate: it keeps only the structure that matters for decisions; it is not the territory itself.
exact.MSE = (4+16+25)/3 = 15；平方讓 +5 與 -5 同樣被懲罰: MSE = (4+16+25)/3 = 15; squaring penalizes +5 and -5 equally, and makes the cost of large errors grow sharply.
exact.NFL：沒有「等差」這個先入為主，下一個是 8、100 或長頸鹿在數學上皆可能。: NFL: without the preconception that the sequence is arithmetic, the next item could mathematically be 8, 100, or a giraffe.

64af8ec5dc9e.zh:
你手上的地圖，
就是馬路本身嗎？ Is the map in your hand the road itself? If every map is "false", what makes a map "good"?
64af8ec5dc9e.en:
Is the map in your hand
the road itself? If every map is “false”, what makes a map “good”?

5d1b3268daf7.zh: 每張地圖都是假的，但有些地圖能帶你買到炸雞、有些讓你掉進許願池。Every map is false — good maps explain now and predict next.
5d1b3268daf7.en: Every map is false, but some maps lead you to fried chicken, while others drop you into a wishing fountain.

566456b13e9c.zh: 什麼叫「地圖不是實地」？What does "Map ≠ Territory" mean?
566456b13e9c.en: What does “the map is not the territory” mean?

a99a5af73020.zh: Fig 1 · 雜亂的真實世界 vs 乾淨的替代品 Surrogate (messy reality vs clean surrogate)
a99a5af73020.en: Fig 1 · The messy real world vs. a clean surrogate

e412521309f1.zh:
你打開 Google 地圖，藍色的線是柏油路嗎？灰色方塊是鋼筋水泥嗎？
走進手機螢幕只會撞壞 iPhone。Is the blue line asphalt? No — it's a surrogate.
e412521309f1.en:
You open Google Maps: is the blue line asphalt? Are the gray blocks steel and concrete?
Try walking into your phone screen and all you'll do is smash your iPhone.

9bf393a002f7.zh: 替代品 (Surrogate)：真實世界有百萬片樹葉、坑洞、野貓打架，地圖全部忽略，只留下「路在哪裡」。Surrogate: ignore noise, keep decision-relevant structure.
9bf393a002f7.en: Surrogate: the real world has millions of leaves, potholes, and stray cats fighting; the map ignores all of it and keeps only “where the road is.”

a6ff9e3fdb3c.zh: 機器學習的模型 (Model) 就是同一回事：世界充滿混亂與雜訊，我們做不出一顆「等於宇宙本身」的水晶球，只能做一張夠用的地圖。Models are maps of chaos — useful, not identical.
a6ff9e3fdb3c.en: A machine-learning model is exactly the same thing: the world is full of chaos and noise, and we can't build a crystal ball that “equals the universe itself”; all we can do is make a map that is good enough.

6844c37f88ba.zh: 地圖把「會不會跌倒」簡化成「這裡有坑請繞路」；模型把「明天下不下雨」簡化成「氣壓+濕度的函數」。Simplify to what matters for decisions.
6844c37f88ba.en: A map simplifies “will I trip?” into “there's a pothole here, please go around”; a model simplifies “will it rain tomorrow?” into “a function of air pressure + humidity.”

a3c922ad2bf0.zh: 什麼才叫「好地圖」？What makes a map "good"?

9132f4fdfae3.zh: 既然每張地圖都是假的，評判標準只剩兩件事。If all maps are false, judge them by two things.
9132f4fdfae3.en: Since every map is false anyway, only two criteria are left for judging one.

b278f0d0f484.zh: ① 能解釋現在 (Explain Now)

536b8f1b5f89.zh: 你站在校門口，地圖能標出「你就在校門口」。You’re at the gate — map marks it correctly.
536b8f1b5f89.en: You're standing at the school gate, and the map can mark “you are at the school gate.”

5d86e1de1fb6.zh: 對應：訓練誤差 (Training Error) 低fits observed data

344a65e011c2.zh: 反面：連自己看過的考題都答錯的地圖，別信fails on seen data → useless
344a65e011c2.en: Flip side: a map that gets even the exam questions it has already seen wrong is not to be trusted

fee519e9f84c.zh: 陷阱：死背答案也能低訓練誤差memorization ≠ understanding
fee519e9f84c.en: Trap: rote-memorizing the answers can also give low training error

7ed455819281.zh: ② 能預測未來 (Predict Next)

e417faf9e5cb.zh: 地圖說「右轉 50m 有炸雞」，你真的買到炸雞。Map says “50m right for fried chicken” — you get it.
e417faf9e5cb.en: The map says “turn right, 50 m, fried chicken,” and you really do get your fried chicken.

746836e83627.zh: 對應：測試誤差 (Test Error) 低 / 泛化 (Generalization) 強works on unseen data
746836e83627.en: Corresponds to: low test error / strong generalization

28f394cd2f04.zh: 反面：照地圖走卻掉進許願池 = 過擬合overfitting = great map, wrong world
28f394cd2f04.en: Flip side: following the map and falling into the wishing well = overfitting

33190e208c8f.zh: 關鍵：這才是科學要的「預測力」prediction is the real test
33190e208c8f.en: Key: this is the “predictive power” science is after

83d70c08a513.zh: 好地圖 = 同時通過「解釋力」與「預測力」的替代品；機器學習要的就是這個。Good map = low training error + low test error.
83d70c08a513.en: Good map = a surrogate that passes both the “explanatory power” test and the “predictive power” test; that is exactly what machine learning wants.

8968947ab4a2.zh: 波普爾怎麼看科學？Popper on Science

2d04f79bd4c8.zh: 科學不是呆坐路邊看螞蟻爬、突然大徹大悟；科學是先大膽地猜一個規律，然後拿現實去拼命打臉它。打不死的猜想，就暫時留著用。Science = bold conjecture + severe attempts to refute. Survivors stay.
2d04f79bd4c8.en: Science is not sitting by the roadside watching ants crawl until you suddenly reach enlightenment; science is boldly guessing a law first, then using reality to try as hard as possible to slap it down. A guess that can't be knocked down gets kept and used, for now.

79a544faf5b0.zh: 先丟出一個候選函數 $f$：「我猜世界長這樣」。Propose a candidate $f$: "world looks like this".
79a544faf5b0.en: First, throw out a candidate function $f$: “I guess the world looks like this.”

5bc0e34ef1a3.zh: 用資料檢驗：猜錯就扣分（損失變大），猜對就加分。Test against data; loss measures mismatch.
5bc0e34ef1a3.en: Test it against data: a wrong guess loses points (the loss goes up), a right guess gains points.

81ab1d35c875.zh: 這正是機器學習的靈魂：假設 → 評分 → 搜尋，不斷猜、打臉、修正。That's ML: hypothesize → score → search.
81ab1d35c875.en: This is the very soul of machine learning: hypothesize → score → search, guessing, getting slapped down, and correcting, over and over.

2e2c07dfb84a.zh: 機器學習三部曲：開菜單、請評委、抓戰犯The Three Steps: Hypothesize · Score · Search
2e2c07dfb84a.en: The three steps of machine learning: write the menu, call in the judges, find the culprit

227690e14bb5.zh: 從線性迴歸到大型語言模型，全世界所有機器學習只有這三步。From linear regression to LLMs — only three steps.
227690e14bb5.en: From linear regression to large language models, all machine learning in the world comes down to just these three steps.

e6dc6f2356a0.zh:
假設空間 $\mathcal{F}$
Hypothesis Class
e6dc6f2356a0.en:
Hypothesis space $\mathcal{F}$
Hypothesis class

f87484d3af24.zh: 決定菜單上有什麼：直線？決策樹？神經網路？Menu of candidates: lines? trees? nets?
f87484d3af24.en: Decide what's on the menu: straight lines? Decision trees? Neural networks?

db3d8a9b3879.zh:
評分機制 $S(f)$
Loss Function
db3d8a9b3879.en:
Scoring mechanism $S(f)$
Loss function

565b142c0e41.zh: 毒舌評審打分：分數越低 = 錯得越不離譜。Loss: lower = less wrong.
565b142c0e41.en: A sharp-tongued judge hands out scores: the lower the score = the less outrageously wrong.

7a60a5ec89b1.zh: 摸黑走下山谷，把罪孽值最低的 $f$ 抓出來。Search loss landscape for minimum.
7a60a5ec89b1.en: Feel your way down the valley in the dark and catch the $f$ with the lowest sin score.

c94fb09785e0.zh: 熱炒店 vs 義大利餐廳 = 你先決定「世界大概長什麼樣」；評審試吃 = 損失函數；抓戰犯 = 最佳化找到最好吃那道。Pick cuisine → judges score → crown winner.
c94fb09785e0.en: Taiwanese stir-fry joint vs. Italian restaurant = you first decide “roughly what the world looks like”; the judges' tasting = the loss function; finding the culprit = optimization finding the tastiest dish.

b94a09725926.zh: 第一步：假設空間 $\mathcal{F}$ — 決定菜單上有什麼Step 1: Hypothesis Class $\mathcal{F}$
b94a09725926.en: Step 1: Hypothesis class $\mathcal{F}$ — decide what's on the menu

b64a1d20c152.zh: 符號先講白話 · Notation in Plain Words

65f85a2fad73.zh: 花體 $\mathcal{F}$ 就是「候選函數的大菜單」；$f \in \mathcal{F}$ 表示「這道菜 $f$ 在菜單裡」。$\mathcal{F}$ = menu; $f \in \mathcal{F}$ = dish on menu.
65f85a2fad73.en: The calligraphic $\mathcal{F}$ is just “the big menu of candidate functions”; $f \in \mathcal{F}$ means “this dish $f$ is on the menu.”

2a72f438dc01.zh: $$ \mathcal{F} = \{ f : \text{所有你願意考慮的函數} \} $$
2a72f438dc01.en: $$ \mathcal{F} = \{ f : \text{all the functions you are willing to consider} \} $$

cc0ba644e56e.zh: 你一開始對世界的「成見」就寫在這裡。Your prior bias lives here.
cc0ba644e56e.en: Your initial “preconceptions” about the world are written right here.

04b610c0d3f5.zh: 「輸入跟輸出成正比的直線」。Assume straight-line relation.
04b610c0d3f5.en: “A straight line where output is proportional to input.”

008452d5670d.zh: 一層一層做二分法：「是/否」切割空間。Hierarchical yes/no splits.
008452d5670d.en: Splits in two, level by level: carves up the space with “yes/no” questions.

61dca9a1b6b3.zh: 多層特徵組合，階層抽象。Layered abstraction.
61dca9a1b6b3.en: Combines features over many layers, abstracting level by level.

c6315a87604f.zh: 菜單越大不一定越好；越大越容易「挑到只會背答案的菜」— 這就是之後的過擬合伏筆。Larger $\mathcal{F}$ ≠ better; bigger menu → easier to overfit.
c6315a87604f.en: A bigger menu isn't necessarily better; the bigger it is, the easier it is to “pick a dish that only memorizes the answers” — this foreshadows overfitting, coming later.

74dea38cb0a6.zh: 第二步：評分機制 $S(f)$ — 毒舌評審來打分Step 2: Scoring $S(f)$ — Loss Function
74dea38cb0a6.en: Step 2: Scoring Mechanism $S(f)$ — The Harsh Judge Hands Out Scores

01bc8847aab3.zh: 候選模型那麼多，誰是天選之子？需要一個打分標準：損失函數 (Loss) — 分數越低越好，因為它衡量「你錯得多離譜」。Loss measures how wrong; lower is better.
01bc8847aab3.en: With so many candidate models, which one is the chosen one? We need a scoring standard: the loss function — the lower the score, the better, because it measures “how badly you're wrong.”

40bf1ce8c458.zh: 均方誤差 MSE · Mean Squared Error

bd0b30f99c02.zh: 白話：每個人「猜錯的距離」先平方（讓正負都變正、離譜的錯加倍懲罰），再平均。Square each error (erase sign, amplify big misses), then average.
bd0b30f99c02.en: In plain words: first square each person's “miss distance” (so positive and negative errors all become positive, and outrageous errors get punished extra hard), then take the average.

5e0b83511f6d.zh: $y_i$ 真實分數、$\hat{y}_i$ 預測分數、$n$ 人數。$y_i$ true, $\hat y_i$ predicted, $n$ count.
5e0b83511f6d.en: $y_i$ is the true score, $\hat{y}_i$ the predicted score, and $n$ the number of people.

db6b6600d0f7.zh: 實例算給你看：三位同學的罪孽值Worked Example: MSE = 15
db6b6600d0f7.en: Worked Example: The Sin Scores of Three Classmates

675946e10957.zh: Fig 2 · 平方誤差長條圖：$4+16+25$ 平均為 $15$ (squared errors averaged)
675946e10957.en: Fig 2 · Bar chart of squared errors: $4+16+25$ averages to $15$

950e09f9a2aa.zh: 這個 $15$ 就是模型 $f$ 的「罪孽值」。下一步：想辦法讓它更小！This 15 is $f$'s loss — now minimize it.
950e09f9a2aa.en: This $15$ is model $f$'s “sin score.” Next step: find a way to make it smaller!

17df5d1bc3c4.zh: 為什麼平方？① 負號消失（$+5$ 與 $-5$ 都是錯）② 大錯重罰：$5^2=25$ 比 $2^2=4$ 痛六倍。Why square? erase sign + punish big errors.
17df5d1bc3c4.en: Why square? ① The minus sign disappears ($+5$ and $-5$ are both errors). ② Big errors get heavy penalties: $5^2=25$ hurts six times as much as $2^2=4$.

de50231da87b.zh: 第三步：最佳化搜尋 — 摸黑走下山谷Step 3: Optimization — Walk Down the Valley
de50231da87b.en: Step 3: Optimization Search — Feeling Your Way Down the Valley in the Dark

d8847a3314fa.zh: 那個嚇人的公式，白話翻譯
d8847a3314fa.en: That scary formula, translated into plain words

a98b40c31861.zh: 請從菜單 $\mathcal{F}$ 裡，把能讓損失 $S(f)$ 縮到最小（$\min$）的模型抓出來（$\arg$），封為 $\hat{f}$（最棒的那道菜）。Pick $f$ in menu that minimizes loss; call it $\hat f$.
a98b40c31861.en: From the menu $\mathcal{F}$, pick out ($\arg$) the model that shrinks the loss $S(f)$ to its minimum ($\min$), and crown it $\hat{f}$ (the very best dish).

c6af5f440817.zh: 記號：$\arg\min$ 回傳「誰最小」；$\min$ 回傳「最小值是多少」。我們要的是冠軍本身，不是分數。$\arg\min$ returns who; $\min$ returns value.
c6af5f440817.en: Notation: $\arg\min$ returns “who is the smallest”; $\min$ returns “what the smallest value is.” What we want is the champion itself, not its score.

59141a04fb6b.zh: Fig 3 · 左：平滑碗（凸）高效求解；右：崎嶇山脈（非凸）需梯度下降 (convex vs non-convex)
59141a04fb6b.en: Fig 3 · Left: a smooth bowl (convex), solved efficiently; right: a rugged mountain range (non-convex), which needs gradient descent

eefa700c5e61.zh: 地形決定方法 · Terrain decides method

aa79c2a26884.zh: 凸最佳化 (Convex)：像平滑的碗，往下滑一定到谷底 → 有解析解 / 高效求解器。Bowl → slide to bottom.
aa79c2a26884.en: Convex optimization: like a smooth bowl, sliding downhill is guaranteed to reach the bottom → closed-form solutions / efficient solvers.

f86cde8ba4ab.zh: 非凸 (Non-convex)：九彎十八拐的山脈（如神經網路）→ 閉眼用腳探哪邊較低，一步一步往下，即梯度下降 (Gradient Descent)。Rugged → step by steepest descent.
f86cde8ba4ab.en: Non-convex: a mountain range full of twists and turns (like a neural network) → close your eyes, feel with your feet which side is lower, and go down one step at a time. That is gradient descent.

a3605ab3976a.zh: 把損失想成海拔：你在濃霧的山中，只能感覺腳下坡度（梯度），就往最陡的下坡跨一小步，重複直到平地。Feel slope under feet, step downhill.
a3605ab3976a.en: Think of the loss as altitude: you're in the mountains in thick fog and can only feel the slope under your feet (the gradient), so you take a small step in the steepest downhill direction, and repeat until you reach flat ground.

bc78280b343b.zh: 梯度下降模擬 · Gradient Descent Simulation — Loss 隨步數下降 (loss vs steps)
bc78280b343b.en: Gradient Descent Simulation — the loss decreases with the number of steps

1a03a25622dc.zh: 沒有免費午餐：沒有成見，就沒有智慧No Free Lunch: No Bias, No Learning
1a03a25622dc.en: No Free Lunch: No Bias, No Intelligence

f976d7ddcbc8.zh: Fig 4 · $2,4,6$ 下一個是 $8$？$100$？還是長頸鹿？(2,4,6 → next?)
f976d7ddcbc8.en: Fig 4 · After $2,4,6$, is the next one $8$? $100$? Or a giraffe?

50d19a8917ea.zh: 定理白話 · Theorem in Plain Words

6f574e9790cc.zh: 沒有免費午餐定理 (No Free Lunch Theorem)：若對問題不做任何先驗假設，不存在一個演算法能在所有問題上都表現優異。No universal winner without assumptions.
6f574e9790cc.en: No Free Lunch theorem: if you make no prior assumptions about the problem, there is no algorithm that performs well on all problems.

c6b64373f079.zh: 看到 $2,4,6$，你直覺猜 $8$（等差）。但若沒有「這是等差數列」的歸納偏置 (Inductive Bias)，下一個也可以是 $100$、或一隻長頸鹿 — 資料本身不告訴你。Without "arithmetic" bias, data says nothing.
c6b64373f079.en: Seeing $2,4,6$, you intuitively guess $8$ (an arithmetic progression). But without the inductive bias that “this is an arithmetic sequence,” the next one could just as well be $100$, or a giraffe — the data itself doesn't tell you.

0ed70f93a259.zh: 直覺的 $8$ 正是你偷偷加進去的成見。Your $8$ is hidden bias.
0ed70f93a259.en: That intuitive $8$ is exactly the bias you secretly slipped in.

f1c9b9490b39.zh: 別想找一把能開全天下所有鎖的萬能鑰匙；大膽施加合理的成見，才是演算法有威力的關鍵。Don't seek a master key; pick the right bias.
f1c9b9490b39.en: Don't go looking for a master key that opens every lock in the world; boldly imposing a reasonable bias is the key to an algorithm's power.

74bbff28ad7d.zh: 機器學習不是消除偏見，而是選對偏見ML is not to remove bias, but to choose it
74bbff28ad7d.en: Machine learning isn't about eliminating bias; it's about choosing the right bias

283c2dd6d46d.zh: 理想 AI 完全客觀、沒有預設立場fully objective, no assumption
283c2dd6d46d.en: The ideal AI is perfectly objective, with no preconceptions

a6236f5c198a.zh: 資料自己會說話data speaks for itself

8608fe9564fd.zh: 結果：寸步難行（2,4,6 怎麼猜都可）paralysis: anything goes
8608fe9564fd.en: Result: you can't take a single step (any guess after 2, 4, 6 is equally valid)

03593742c596.zh: 歸納偏置 (Inductive Bias) = 先猜世界長什麼樣prior guess on world shape
03593742c596.en: Inductive bias = first guessing what the world looks like

9e9b05b02b65.zh: 假設空間 $\mathcal{F}$ 就是把偏置寫下來$\mathcal{F}$ encodes your bias
9e9b05b02b65.en: The hypothesis space $\mathcal{F}$ is that bias written down

42c6216bb347.zh: 結果：有成見才有泛化能力bias → generalization
42c6216bb347.en: Result: only with preconceptions can a model generalize

5c330c35657b.zh: 呼應波普爾：科學從「大膽猜」開始；機器學習從「選 $\mathcal{F}$」開始。Science starts with conjecture; ML starts with $\mathcal{F}$.
5c330c35657b.en: Echoing Popper: science starts with a “bold guess”; machine learning starts with “choosing $\mathcal{F}$”.

78db8fc41957.zh: 總覽：從假設到泛化的完整迴圈Overview: Full Loop from Hypothesis to Generalization
78db8fc41957.en: Overview: the complete loop from hypothesis to generalization

5aed9cf89286.zh: 把四個盒子連成一個會呼吸的迴圈。Connect four boxes into a breathing loop.
5aed9cf89286.en: Connect the four boxes into a loop that breathes.

1c2765e8a900.zh: 機器學習學習迴圈：假設 · 評分 · 搜尋 · 泛化
1c2765e8a900.en: The ML learning loop: hypothesize · score · search · generalize

d74b2dc5d0be.zh: 「模型是地圖，不是實地」— 從假設空間到真實世界預測
d74b2dc5d0be.en: “The model is the map, not the territory”: from hypothesis space to real-world prediction

1344161a401f.zh: • 候選函數集合 f ∈ F

bc7e59262391.zh: 怎麼讀這張圖 · How to read

feb8a70df6ce.zh: 外層虛線框 = 歸納偏置的約束範疇；$1\to2\to3$ 是正向流程；$3\to$泛化是輸出；泛化失敗的虛線箭頭回到假設 — 這就是「學習迴圈」。Outer dashed = bias scope; solid = forward; dashed back = revise when generalization fails.
feb8a70df6ce.en: Outer dashed box = the scope constrained by the inductive bias; $1\to2\to3$ is the forward flow; $3\to$ generalization is the output; the dashed arrow from a generalization failure back to the hypothesis: that is the “learning loop”.

ac53f79bf65a.zh: 泛化與過擬合：為什麼只背答案會考砸？Generalization & Overfitting
ac53f79bf65a.en: Generalization and overfitting: why does just memorizing answers make you bomb the exam?

d7bf56e94fd5.zh: 訓練誤差低不代表學會了；像「把考古題答案背起來」的人，換張考卷就露餡。Low training error ≠ learned; memorizing past exams fails on new paper.
d7bf56e94fd5.en: Low training error doesn't mean the model has learned; like someone who memorized the answers to past exams, it gets exposed as soon as the exam paper changes.

f246d4ee6536.zh: 模型複雜度 vs 誤差 · Model Complexity vs Error — 訓練誤差持續降、測試誤差先降後升 (overfitting valley)
f246d4ee6536.en: Model complexity vs. error: training error keeps falling, while test error first falls and then rises (the overfitting valley)

0b1fb933406b.zh: 測試誤差最低點：既解釋現在、又預測未來。Test error minimum = good map.
0b1fb933406b.en: The lowest point of the test error: it both explains the present and predicts the future.

f7cfe54090f0.zh: 訓練誤差持續降、測試誤差飆升：地圖把「坑洞的形狀」也當成「路」。Fits noise as if it's signal.
f7cfe54090f0.en: Training error keeps falling while test error shoots up: the map treats even “the shape of the potholes” as “the road”.

eb81d7a2f9ab.zh: 下一步路線圖Roadmap — Where to next?

c1e71799c49f.zh: 菜單太窄 = 偏差高（看不見真相）；菜單太寬 = 變異高（把雜訊當真相）。Too narrow = bias; too wide = variance.
c1e71799c49f.en: Menu too narrow = high bias (can't see the truth); menu too wide = high variance (mistakes noise for the truth).

0122904480cc.zh: 用驗證集當「模擬考」，用正則化懲罰過度複雜的 $f$。Mock exam + penalize complexity.
0122904480cc.en: Use a validation set as a “mock exam”, and use regularization to penalize an overly complex $f$.

3941e8010ad4.zh: Q1. 為什麼說「地圖不是實地」？哪個選項最貼近講義原意？Why "map ≠ territory"? Which captures the idea?
3941e8010ad4.en: Q1. Why do we say “the map is not the territory”? Which option comes closest to what the notes mean?

f7d0a004e33c.zh: A. 地圖畫得不夠漂亮 (map not pretty)
f7d0a004e33c.en: A. The map isn’t drawn nicely enough

491f17045891.zh: B. 模型是對真實世界的簡化替代品，有用但不等於真相 (surrogate, useful not identical)
491f17045891.en: B. A model is a simplified surrogate for the real world: useful, but not the same as the truth

6efc10ca4409.zh: C. 地圖一定比實地小張 (map smaller)
6efc10ca4409.en: C. A map is always smaller than the territory

fe25a6aa61f6.zh: D. 實地會隨時間消失 (territory vanishes)
fe25a6aa61f6.en: D. The territory disappears over time

a3ceca7f3023.zh: Q2. 用講義的 MSE 例子：$y=[80,90,70]$, $\hat y=[82,86,75]$，MSE 是多少？為什麼要平方？MSE? Why square?
a3ceca7f3023.en: Q2. Using the MSE example from the notes: $y=[80,90,70]$, $\hat y=[82,86,75]$, what is the MSE? Why do we square the errors?

8ff3a3d5d240.zh: A. 15.2，因為要讓數字變大 (make bigger)
8ff3a3d5d240.en: A. 15.2, because it makes the numbers bigger

598ad2b34eac.zh: B. 15，因為直接平均誤差 (average raw error)
598ad2b34eac.en: B. 15, because it just averages the errors directly

5e923ddbe12f.zh: C. 15，因為 $(4+16+25)/3$；平方消除正負並放大大錯 ($4+16+25)/3; erase sign, amplify big errors
5e923ddbe12f.en: C. 15, because $(4+16+25)/3$; squaring removes the sign and amplifies large errors

b46e2a971094.zh: D. 45，因為加總就好 (sum only)
b46e2a971094.en: D. 45, because you just add them up

4136e0fc9115.zh: Q3. 沒有免費午餐定理在說什麼？看到 $2,4,6$ 為什麼不能確定下一個是 $8$？No Free Lunch: why 2,4,6 → 8 not guaranteed?
4136e0fc9115.en: Q3. What does the No Free Lunch theorem say? When you see $2,4,6$, why can’t you be sure the next one is $8$?

f2e45d8ae9da.zh: A. 沒有「等差數列」的歸納偏置，資料本身允許任何下一個值 (no bias → anything goes)
f2e45d8ae9da.en: A. Without the inductive bias “it’s an arithmetic sequence”, the data by itself allows any next value

c3cbc539221b.zh: B. 因為 $8$ 算錯了，應該是 $10$ ($8$ miscalc.)
c3cbc539221b.en: B. Because $8$ is a miscalculation; it should be $10$

cbdf045e5631.zh: C. 因為機器學習只能處理圖片 (only images)
cbdf045e5631.en: C. Because machine learning can only handle images

e56e074880bf.zh: D. 因為資料太少，永遠無解 (too little data, hopeless)
e56e074880bf.en: D. Because there is too little data, so it can never be solved

42f963268285.zh:
選一個合適的成見，
去理解這個世界。 Pick the right bias to understand the world. Models aren't truth — good maps predict.
42f963268285.en:
Pick the right bias,
and use it to understand the world. Models aren't truth — good maps predict.
